**My reasoning:**

I have been working this land for over forty years. My father planted wheat and maize, I plant wheat and maize, and that is what I know. Here in Quzhou the soil is good for the two-crop system — winter wheat then summer maize on the same fields. I have about 8 mu I can still manage myself. My knees are not what they were, so I will not take on more.

I will not try any new crops. Last year my neighbor tried something different and had trouble selling it. I do not need that headache at my age. Wheat I can sell at the grain station without worry. Maize too.

For seed I buy whatever the seed shop in town is selling this year — they usually have the improved wheat variety everyone uses around here, Kenong 199 or similar. For maize I will get the hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, same as always. Everyone uses it.

For fertilizer I put down diammonium phosphate and urea as base before planting the wheat, then top-dress urea in spring at jointing. My neighbor's son told me I use too much nitrogen but I would rather have a good harvest. I do not buy much potassium — never have, my father never did either.

I irrigate the wheat three times: before sowing to moisten the soil, again at jointing, and at heading. For maize I irrigate at silking if there is no rain.

After wheat harvest I will plant maize directly — no ploughing, the machine does it all in one pass now. That saves my back.

I spray herbicide on the wheat in winter and fungicide before heading. For maize I spray once for weeds and once if I see corn borer.
